manifest.title: The local realization of generating series of finite Lie rank

inputs.abstract:
A real noncommutative generating series admits a finite-dimensional analytic
differential representation if and only if its Lie rank is finite and it
satisfies the convergence condition on ordered products of Lie polynomials.
The Lie rank is the least representation dimension. Two representations
of that dimension are equivalent by an analytic change of coordinates
fixing the origin.

The algebraic foundation consists of shuffle multiplication, the
Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt theorem, and formal coordinates on the annihilator
of a finite-codimension Lie subalgebra. The analytic argument uses
factorial estimates for iterated vector fields, convergence of residual
series, and the analytic inverse function theorem. Convergence is expressed
by geometric bounds on commutative power-series coefficients. Both the
output and all vector-field coefficients are required to converge.

The submission includes the real-coefficient algebraic foundation and its
proofs, so it has no dependencies on other archive submissions. The source
paper records the three approved corrections to the analytic statements
and estimates.

concepts.title: Calculus of convergent power series
concepts.description:
The geometric coefficient bound is equivalent to absolute summability at
some positive polyradius. Convergent series form a real subalgebra and are
closed under partial differentiation.

A formally continuous algebra homomorphism sending each variable to a
convergent series with zero constant term preserves convergence. This is
composition of convergent power series at the origin.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.ConvergentSeries
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecificLimits.Normed
import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Subalgebra.Basic

/-!
---
title: Calculus of convergent power series
type: theorem
---
The geometric coefficient bound is equivalent to absolute summability at
some positive polyradius. Convergent series form a real subalgebra and are
closed under partial differentiation.

A formally continuous algebra homomorphism sending each variable to a
convergent series with zero constant term preserves convergence. This is
composition of convergent power series at the origin.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.AnalyticCalculus

open Lax825748.FormalSeries Lax825748.Monomials ConvergentSeries

axiom absolute_convergence {d : ℕ} (f : StateSeries d) :
  Convergent f ↔ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧
    Summable (fun I : Fin d →₀ ℕ => |MvPowerSeries.coeff I f| * r ^ totalDegree I)

axiom subalgebra (d : ℕ) :
  ∃ A : Subalgebra ℝ (StateSeries d), ∀ f, f ∈ A ↔ Convergent f

axiom partial_derivative {d : ℕ} (f : StateSeries d) (hf : Convergent f)
    (i : Fin d) :
  Convergent (MvPowerSeries.pderiv ℝ i f)

axiom composition {d e : ℕ} (φ : StateSeries d →ₐ[ℝ] StateSeries e)
    (hc : FormallyContinuous φ)
    (h0 : ∀ i, MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (φ (MvPowerSeries.X i)) = 0)
    (hφ : ∀ i, Convergent (φ (MvPowerSeries.X i)))
    (f : StateSeries d) (hf : Convergent f) :
  Convergent (φ f)

end Lax825748.AnalyticCalculus

statements.signature:
absolute_convergence : ∀ {d : Nat} (f : Lax825748.FormalSeries.StateSeries d),
  Iff (Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.Convergent f)
    (Exists fun r =>
      And (Real.instLT.lt 0 r)
        (Summable fun I =>
          instHMul.hMul (abs (LinearMap.instFunLike.coe (MvPowerSeries.coeff I) f))
            (instHPow.hPow r (Lax825748.Monomials.totalDegree (Finsupp.instFunLike.coe I)))))

composition : ∀ {d e : Nat} (φ : AlgHom Real (Lax825748.FormalSeries.StateSeries d) (Lax825748.FormalSeries.StateSeries e)),
  Lax825748.FormalSeries.FormallyContinuous (AlgHom.funLike.coe φ) →
    (∀ (i : Fin d),
        Eq (RingHom.instFunLike.coe MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (AlgHom.funLike.coe φ (MvPowerSeries.X i))) 0) →
      (∀ (i : Fin d), Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.Convergent (AlgHom.funLike.coe φ (MvPowerSeries.X i))) →
        ∀ (f : Lax825748.FormalSeries.StateSeries d),
          Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.Convergent f → Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.Convergent (AlgHom.funLike.coe φ f)

partial_derivative : ∀ {d : Nat} (f : Lax825748.FormalSeries.StateSeries d),
  Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.Convergent f →
    ∀ (i : Fin d), Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.Convergent (Derivation.instFunLike.coe (MvPowerSeries.pderiv Real i) f)

subalgebra : ∀ (d : Nat),
  Exists fun A =>
    ∀ (f : Lax825748.FormalSeries.StateSeries d),
      Iff (SetLike.instMembership.mem A f) (Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.Convergent f)

concepts.title: Analytic changes of coordinates
concepts.description:
An analytic change of coordinates is a formally continuous real algebra
automorphism fixing the origin whose coordinate images, in both directions,
are convergent power series.

The analytic inverse function theorem implies that a formal change of
coordinates with convergent coordinate images has convergent inverse images.
This is the implicit function theorem used in part b) of the paper.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.ConvergentSeries
import Lax825748.CoordinateChange

/-!
---
title: Analytic changes of coordinates
type: theorem
---
An analytic change of coordinates is a formally continuous real algebra
automorphism fixing the origin whose coordinate images, in both directions,
are convergent power series.

The analytic inverse function theorem implies that a formal change of
coordinates with convergent coordinate images has convergent inverse images.
This is the implicit function theorem used in part b) of the paper.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.AnalyticChanges

open Lax825748.FormalSeries Lax825748.CoordinateChange ConvergentSeries

structure AnalyticChange (d : ℕ) extends FormalChange d where
  convergent_toFun : ∀ i, Convergent (toAlgEquiv (MvPowerSeries.X i))
  convergent_invFun : ∀ i, Convergent (toAlgEquiv.symm (MvPowerSeries.X i))

axiom inverse_convergent {d : ℕ} (φ : FormalChange d)
    (hφ : ∀ i, Convergent (φ.toAlgEquiv (MvPowerSeries.X i))) :
  ∀ i, Convergent (φ.toAlgEquiv.symm (MvPowerSeries.X i))

end Lax825748.AnalyticChanges

  (∀ (i : Fin d), Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.Convergent (AlgEquiv.instFunLike.coe φ.toAlgEquiv (MvPowerSeries.X i))) →
    ∀ (i : Fin d),
      Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.Convergent (AlgEquiv.instFunLike.coe φ.toAlgEquiv.symm (MvPowerSeries.X i))

concepts.title: Convergent coordinates on an annihilator
concepts.description:
Let $T_1,\ldots,T_d$ be normalized, zero-constant coordinates on $J^\perp$
as in Proposition 1, each satisfying (C). Every element of $J^\perp$
satisfying (C) is a convergent series in the $T_i$.

Indeed, the $T_i$ are convergent series in PBW coordinates and have
identity linear part. Their inverse change of coordinates is convergent
by the analytic inverse function theorem.

import Lax825748.PBWConvergence
import Lax825748.AnalyticCalculus
import Lax825748.AnalyticChanges

/-!
---
title: Convergent coordinates on an annihilator
type: theorem
---
Let $T_1,\ldots,T_d$ be normalized, zero-constant coordinates on $J^\perp$
as in Proposition 1, each satisfying (C). Every element of $J^\perp$
satisfying (C) is a convergent series in the $T_i$.

Indeed, the $T_i$ are convergent series in PBW coordinates and have

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.AnalyticCoordinates

open Lax825748.Series Lax825748.LieRank Lax825748.Annihilator
open Lax825748.FormalSeries ConvergentSeries

axiom expansion_converges {X : Type} {d : ℕ}
    (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X) (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X)
    (hP : IsComplement K P) (T : Fin d → NCSeries X)
    (hT : IsCoordinateFamily K P T)
    (hCT : ∀ i, ConvergenceHypothesis.Holds (T i))
    (U : NCSeries X) (hU : InAnnihilator K U)
    (hCU : ConvergenceHypothesis.Holds U) :
  ∃ f : StateSeries d, Convergent f ∧ substituteShuffle T f = U

end Lax825748.AnalyticCoordinates

statements.signature:
expansion_converges : ∀ {X : Type} {d : Nat} (K : Lax825748.Annihilator.LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
  (P : Fin d → Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
  Lax825748.Annihilator.IsComplement K P →
    ∀ (T : Fin d → Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
      Lax825748.Annihilator.IsCoordinateFamily K P T →
        (∀ (i : Fin d), Lax825748.ConvergenceHypothesis.Holds (T i)) →
          ∀ (U : Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
            Lax825748.Annihilator.InAnnihilator K U →
              Lax825748.ConvergenceHypothesis.Holds U →
                Exists fun f =>
                  And (Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.Convergent f) (Eq (Lax825748.Annihilator.substituteShuffle T f) U)

concepts.title: Analytic differential representations
concepts.description:
A differential representation is analytic if its output series and every
coefficient of each of its vector fields converge near the origin.
Its generated coefficient at a word $w$ is the constant term of $h\mu w$,
with the vector fields acting on the right in the order of the letters.
A series is analytically produced if such a representation exists in some
finite dimension, including dimension zero.

Convergence of the vector fields is required explicitly. It is used in
the proof and in the interpretation by analytic systems, although omitted
from the printed Definition 1.

namespace Lax825748.AnalyticRepresentations

open Lax825748.Series Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation ConvergentSeries

def IsAnalytic {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (R : Representation X d) : Prop :=
  Convergent R.output ∧ ∀ x i, Convergent (R.fields x i)

def AnalyticallyProduced {X : Type} (g : NCSeries X) : Prop :=
  ∃ d, ∃ R : Representation X d, IsAnalytic R ∧ Represents R g

end Lax825748.AnalyticRepresentations

concepts.title: Formal coordinates on the annihilator of a Lie subalgebra
concepts.description:
Proposition 1. Let $L_0$ be a Lie subalgebra of the Lie polynomials and let
$P_1,\ldots,P_d$ represent a basis modulo $L_0$. Set
$J=\mathbb R\langle X\rangle L_0$. If the zero-constant series $S_i$ vanish
on $J$ and satisfy $(S_i,P_j)=\delta_{ij}$, substitution of the $S_i$ into
commutative formal series is a bijection onto $J^\perp$.

Substitution is defined coefficient by coefficient using a finite truncation:
at a word of length $n$, only monomials of degree at most $n$ contribute.
There exist such coordinates dual to the degree-one PBW monomials. For these
coordinates the coefficient of $S^I$ in $T\in J^\perp$ is $(T,P^I)/I!$.
The annihilator is closed under the shuffle and all right residuals.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.PBW
import Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities
import Lax825748.FormalSeries
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Span

/-!
---
title: Formal coordinates on the annihilator of a Lie subalgebra
type: theorem
---
Proposition 1. Let $L_0$ be a Lie subalgebra of the Lie polynomials and let
$P_1,\ldots,P_d$ represent a basis modulo $L_0$. Set
$J=\mathbb R\langle X\rangle L_0$. If the zero-constant series $S_i$ vanish
on $J$ and satisfy $(S_i,P_j)=\delta_{ij}$, substitution of the $S_i$ into
commutative formal series is a bijection onto $J^\perp$.

Substitution is defined coefficient by coefficient using a finite truncation:
at a word of length $n$, only monomials of degree at most $n$ contribute.
There exist such coordinates dual to the degree-one PBW monomials. For these
coordinates the coefficient of $S^I$ in $T\in J^\perp$ is $(T,P^I)/I!$.
The annihilator is closed under the shuffle and all right residuals.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.Annihilator

open Series LieRank Monomials Shuffle ShuffleIdentities FormalSeries

abbrev LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials (X : Type) := LieSubalgebra ℝ (LiePolynomial X)

noncomputable def generatedIdeal {X : Type} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X) :
    Ideal (NCPolynomial X) :=
  Ideal.span {P | ∃ k : K, P = k.val.val}

def InAnnihilator {X : Type} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X) (S : NCSeries X) : Prop :=
  ∀ P ∈ generatedIdeal K, pairing S P = 0

def IsComplement {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) : Prop :=
  LinearIndependent ℝ (fun i => K.toSubmodule.mkQ (P i)) ∧
    Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun i => K.toSubmodule.mkQ (P i)) = ⊤

def IsCoordinateFamily {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, S i 1 = 0) ∧ (∀ i, InAnnihilator K (S i)) ∧
    ∀ i j, pairing (S i) (P j).val = if i = j then 1 else 0

noncomputable def substituteShuffle {X : Type} {d : ℕ}
    (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) (f : StateSeries d) : NCSeries X :=
  fun w => (AddMonoidAlgebra.coeff
    (MvPowerSeries.truncTotal (w.toList.length + 1) f)).sum
    fun I a => a * shuffleMonomial S I w

def IsPBWCoordinateFamily {X : Type} {d : ℕ}
    (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) : Prop :=
  ∀ i (I : Fin d →₀ ℕ),
    pairing (S i) (orderedPowers (fun j => (P j).val) I) =
      if I = Finsupp.single i 1 then 1 else 0

axiom coordinates_exist {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (hP : IsComplement K P) :
  ∃ S : Fin d → NCSeries X, IsCoordinateFamily K P S ∧ IsPBWCoordinateFamily P S

axiom formal_coordinates {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (hP : IsComplement K P)
    (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) (hS : IsCoordinateFamily K P S) :
  ∀ T : NCSeries X, InAnnihilator K T ↔ ∃! f : StateSeries d, substituteShuffle S f = T

axiom pbw_expansion {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (hP : IsComplement K P)
    (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) (hS : IsCoordinateFamily K P S)
    (hPBW : IsPBWCoordinateFamily P S) (T : NCSeries X) (hT : InAnnihilator K T) :
  ∃ f : StateSeries d, substituteShuffle S f = T ∧
    ∀ I : Fin d →₀ ℕ, MvPowerSeries.coeff I f =
      pairing T (orderedPowers (fun j => (P j).val) I) / (multiFactorial I : ℝ)

axiom closed_shuffle {X : Type} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    (S T : NCSeries X) (hS : InAnnihilator K S) (hT : InAnnihilator K T) :
  InAnnihilator K (shuffle S T)

axiom closed_residual {X : Type} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    (S : NCSeries X) (hS : InAnnihilator K S) (P : NCPolynomial X) :
  InAnnihilator K (rightResidual S P)

end Lax825748.Annihilator

statements.signature:
closed_residual : ∀ {X : Type} (K : Lax825748.Annihilator.LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X) (S : Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
  Lax825748.Annihilator.InAnnihilator K S →
    ∀ (P : Lax825748.Series.NCPolynomial X), Lax825748.Annihilator.InAnnihilator K (Lax825748.Series.rightResidual S P)

closed_shuffle : ∀ {X : Type} (K : Lax825748.Annihilator.LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X) (S T : Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
  Lax825748.Annihilator.InAnnihilator K S →
    Lax825748.Annihilator.InAnnihilator K T → Lax825748.Annihilator.InAnnihilator K (Lax825748.Shuffle.shuffle S T)

coordinates_exist : ∀ {X : Type} {d : Nat} (K : Lax825748.Annihilator.LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
  (P : Fin d → Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
  Lax825748.Annihilator.IsComplement K P →
    Exists fun S =>
      And (Lax825748.Annihilator.IsCoordinateFamily K P S) (Lax825748.Annihilator.IsPBWCoordinateFamily P S)

formal_coordinates : ∀ {X : Type} {d : Nat} (K : Lax825748.Annihilator.LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
  (P : Fin d → Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
  Lax825748.Annihilator.IsComplement K P →
    ∀ (S : Fin d → Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
      Lax825748.Annihilator.IsCoordinateFamily K P S →
        ∀ (T : Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
          Iff (Lax825748.Annihilator.InAnnihilator K T)
            (ExistsUnique fun f => Eq (Lax825748.Annihilator.substituteShuffle S f) T)

pbw_expansion : ∀ {X : Type} {d : Nat} (K : Lax825748.Annihilator.LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
  (P : Fin d → Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
  Lax825748.Annihilator.IsComplement K P →
    ∀ (S : Fin d → Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
      Lax825748.Annihilator.IsCoordinateFamily K P S →
        Lax825748.Annihilator.IsPBWCoordinateFamily P S →
          ∀ (T : Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
            Lax825748.Annihilator.InAnnihilator K T →
              Exists fun f =>
                And (Eq (Lax825748.Annihilator.substituteShuffle S f) T)
                  (∀ (I : Finsupp (Fin d) Nat),
                    Eq (LinearMap.instFunLike.coe (MvPowerSeries.coeff I) f)
                      (instHDiv.hDiv
                        (Lax825748.Series.pairing T
                          (Lax825748.Monomials.orderedPowers (fun j => (P j).val) (Finsupp.instFunLike.coe I)))
                        (Lax825748.Monomials.multiFactorial (Finsupp.instFunLike.coe I)).cast))

concepts.title: Constructible differentially algebraic series
concepts.description:
A commutative formal power series is constructible differentially algebraic
(CDA) if it belongs to a finitely generated unital real subalgebra stable
under every ordinary partial derivative. Auxiliary generators are allowed;
their number need not equal the number of independent variables.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.FormalSeries
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Adjoin.FG

/-!
---
title: Constructible differentially algebraic series
type: definition
---
A commutative formal power series is constructible differentially algebraic
(CDA) if it belongs to a finitely generated unital real subalgebra stable
under every ordinary partial derivative. Auxiliary generators are allowed;
their number need not equal the number of independent variables.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.CDA

open FormalSeries

def DerivativeStable {d : ℕ} (C : Subalgebra ℝ (StateSeries d)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Fin d) (f : StateSeries d), f ∈ C → MvPowerSeries.pderiv ℝ i f ∈ C

def IsCDA {d : ℕ} (f : StateSeries d) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : Subalgebra ℝ (StateSeries d), C.FG ∧ DerivativeStable C ∧ f ∈ C

end Lax825748.CDA

concepts.title: CDA coefficients in minimal formal realizations
concepts.description:
In normalized shuffle-finite coordinates, all elements of the witnessing
shuffle algebra that belong to the coordinate annihilator have expansions
in one finitely generated algebra stable under ordinary partial derivatives.
In particular, a minimal realization has CDA output and CDA vector-field
coefficients, while its coordinate series remain shuffle finite.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.CDA
import Lax825748.ShuffleFiniteCoordinates

/-!
---
title: CDA coefficients in minimal formal realizations
type: theorem
---
In normalized shuffle-finite coordinates, all elements of the witnessing
shuffle algebra that belong to the coordinate annihilator have expansions
in one finitely generated algebra stable under ordinary partial derivatives.
In particular, a minimal realization has CDA output and CDA vector-field
coefficients, while its coordinate series remain shuffle finite.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.CDACoefficients

open Series LieRank Annihilator FormalSeries ShuffleFinite
open DifferentialRepresentation RepresentationMap CDA

axiom coordinate_algebra {X : Type} {k : ℕ}
    (A : ShuffleSubalgebra X) (hfg : FinitelyGenerated A)
    (hstable : ShuffleFinite.DerivativeStable A)
    (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X) (P : Fin k → LiePolynomial X)
    (hP : IsComplement K P) (G : Fin k → NCSeries X)
    (hG : IsCoordinateFamily K P G) (hmem : ∀ i, G i ∈ A.toSubmodule) :
    ∃ C : Subalgebra ℝ (StateSeries k), C.FG ∧ CDA.DerivativeStable C ∧
      ∀ u : StateSeries k, substituteShuffle G u ∈ A.toSubmodule → u ∈ C

axiom minimal_realization {X : Type} [Finite X] (f : NCSeries X) (k : ℕ)
    (hr : HasLieRank f k) (A : ShuffleSubalgebra X)
    (hfg : FinitelyGenerated A) (hstable : ShuffleFinite.DerivativeStable A)
    (hf : f ∈ A.toSubmodule) :
    ∃ R : Representation X k, Represents R f ∧ IsCDA R.output ∧
      (∀ (x : X) (i : Fin k), IsCDA (R.fields x i)) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin k, eta R (MvPowerSeries.X i) ∈ A.toSubmodule ∧
        IsShuffleFinite (eta R (MvPowerSeries.X i))

end Lax825748.CDACoefficients

statements.signature:
coordinate_algebra : ∀ {X : Type} {k : Nat} (A : Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.ShuffleSubalgebra X),
  Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.FinitelyGenerated A →
    Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.DerivativeStable A →
      ∀ (K : Lax825748.Annihilator.LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
        (P : Fin k → Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
        Lax825748.Annihilator.IsComplement K P →
          ∀ (G : Fin k → Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
            Lax825748.Annihilator.IsCoordinateFamily K P G →
              (∀ (i : Fin k), SetLike.instMembership.mem A.toSubmodule (G i)) →
                Exists fun C =>
                  And C.FG
                    (And (Lax825748.CDA.DerivativeStable C)
                      (∀ (u : Lax825748.FormalSeries.StateSeries k),
                        SetLike.instMembership.mem A.toSubmodule (Lax825748.Annihilator.substituteShuffle G u) →
                          SetLike.instMembership.mem C u))

minimal_realization : ∀ {X : Type} [Finite X] (f : Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X) (k : Nat),
  Lax825748.LieRank.HasLieRank f k →
    ∀ (A : Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.ShuffleSubalgebra X),
      Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.FinitelyGenerated A →
        Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.DerivativeStable A →
          SetLike.instMembership.mem A.toSubmodule f →
            Exists fun R =>
              And (Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.Represents R f)
                (And (Lax825748.CDA.IsCDA R.output)
                  (And (∀ (x : X) (i : Fin k), Lax825748.CDA.IsCDA (R.fields x i))
                    (∀ (i : Fin k),
                      And
                        (SetLike.instMembership.mem A.toSubmodule
                          (Lax825748.RepresentationMap.eta R (MvPowerSeries.X i)))
                        (Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.IsShuffleFinite
                          (Lax825748.RepresentationMap.eta R (MvPowerSeries.X i))))))

concepts.title: The convergence hypothesis on Lie polynomials
concepts.description:
Condition (C) requires that, for every finite ordered family of Lie
polynomials $P_1,\ldots,P_q$, there are $\alpha,C>0$ such that
$$|(g,P_1^{i_1}\cdots P_q^{i_q})|\leq\alpha C^{|I|}I!.$$
The constants may depend on the family, but not on the exponents.

The inequalities $I!\leq |I|!\leq q^{|I|}I!$ show that replacing $I!$
by $|I|!$ gives the same condition. Empty families are allowed.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.LieRank
import Lax825748.Monomials

/-!
---
title: The convergence hypothesis on Lie polynomials
type: definition
---
Condition (C) requires that, for every finite ordered family of Lie
polynomials $P_1,\ldots,P_q$, there are $\alpha,C>0$ such that
$$|(g,P_1^{i_1}\cdots P_q^{i_q})|\leq\alpha C^{|I|}I!.$$
The constants may depend on the family, but not on the exponents.

The inequalities $I!\leq |I|!\leq q^{|I|}I!$ show that replacing $I!$
by $|I|!$ gives the same condition. Empty families are allowed.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.ConvergenceHypothesis

open Lax825748.Series Lax825748.LieRank Lax825748.Monomials

def Holds {X : Type} (g : NCSeries X) : Prop :=
  ∀ (q : ℕ) (P : Fin q → LiePolynomial X),
    ∃ α : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ I : Fin q → ℕ,
        |pairing g (orderedPowers (fun j => (P j).val) I)| ≤
          α * C ^ totalDegree I * (multiFactorial I : ℝ)

def HoldsWithTotalFactorial {X : Type} (g : NCSeries X) : Prop :=
  ∀ (q : ℕ) (P : Fin q → LiePolynomial X),
    ∃ α : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ I : Fin q → ℕ,
        |pairing g (orderedPowers (fun j => (P j).val) I)| ≤
          α * C ^ totalDegree I * ((totalDegree I).factorial : ℝ)

axiom factorial_comparison {q : ℕ} (I : Fin q → ℕ) :
  multiFactorial I ≤ (totalDegree I).factorial ∧
    (totalDegree I).factorial ≤ q ^ totalDegree I * multiFactorial I

axiom total_factorial_iff {X : Type} (g : NCSeries X) :
  Holds g ↔ HoldsWithTotalFactorial g

end Lax825748.ConvergenceHypothesis

    (instLENat.le (Lax825748.Monomials.totalDegree I).factorial
      (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow q (Lax825748.Monomials.totalDegree I)) (Lax825748.Monomials.multiFactorial I)))

concepts.title: Convergent commutative power series
concepts.description:
A real power series in $d$ commuting variables is convergent if its
coefficients admit a geometric bound
$|f_I|\leq\alpha C^{|I|}$ with $\alpha,C>0$.
For finitely many variables this is equivalent to absolute convergence
on a neighborhood of the origin. Dimension zero is included.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.FormalSeries

/-!
---
title: Convergent commutative power series
type: definition
---
A real power series in $d$ commuting variables is convergent if its
coefficients admit a geometric bound
$|f_I|\leq\alpha C^{|I|}$ with $\alpha,C>0$.
For finitely many variables this is equivalent to absolute convergence
on a neighborhood of the origin. Dimension zero is included.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.ConvergentSeries

open Lax825748.FormalSeries Lax825748.Monomials

def HasGeometricBound {d : ℕ} (f : StateSeries d) (α C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ I : Fin d →₀ ℕ, |MvPowerSeries.coeff I f| ≤ α * C ^ totalDegree I

def Convergent {d : ℕ} (f : StateSeries d) : Prop :=
  ∃ α : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ HasGeometricBound f α C

end Lax825748.ConvergentSeries

concepts.title: Formal changes of coordinates
concepts.description:
A formal change of coordinates is a real algebra automorphism of
$\mathbb R[[q_1,\ldots,q_d]]$ fixing the origin, continuous in both
directions for the formal topology. Its coordinate images and their inverse
images have zero constant term. Dimension zero is allowed.

concepts.title: Formal differential representations
concepts.description:
A formal differential representation of dimension $d$ consists of one
formal vector field for each letter and an arbitrary formal output series $h$.
The operators act on the right: the word $xy$ applies the field for $x$
first and then the field for $y$. Its generated coefficient at $w$ is
the constant term of $h\mu w$.

Specifying the fields is equivalent to specifying the monoid homomorphism
$\mu$. All state series and vector-field coefficients are formal.

import Lax825748.FormalSeries

/-!
---
title: Formal differential representations
type: definition
---
A formal differential representation of dimension $d$ consists of one
formal vector field for each letter and an arbitrary formal output series $h$.
The operators act on the right: the word $xy$ applies the field for $x$
first and then the field for $y$. Its generated coefficient at $w$ is
the constant term of $h\mu w$.

Specifying the fields is equivalent to specifying the monoid homomorphism
$\mu$. All state series and vector-field coefficients are formal.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation

open Series FormalSeries

structure Representation (X : Type) (d : ℕ) where
  fields : X → VectorField d
  output : StateSeries d

noncomputable def act {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (R : Representation X d)
    (f : StateSeries d) (w : Word X) : StateSeries d :=
  w.toList.foldl (fun k x => applyVectorField (R.fields x) k) f

noncomputable def generatingSeries {X : Type} {d : ℕ}
    (R : Representation X d) : NCSeries X :=
  fun w => MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (act R R.output w)

def Represents {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (R : Representation X d)
    (g : NCSeries X) : Prop := generatingSeries R = g

def DifferentiallyProduced {X : Type} (g : NCSeries X) : Prop :=
  ∃ d, ∃ R : Representation X d, Represents R g

end Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation

concepts.title: Factorial estimates for iterated analytic vector fields
concepts.description:
Suppose the output and all vector-field coefficients admit the same bound
$\alpha C^{|I|}$, where $\alpha,C>0$. For a word of length $p$, its generated
coefficient has absolute value at most $\alpha(2d\alpha C)^p p!$.
Consequently every analytic representation on a finite alphabet has a
uniform factorial bound on its word coefficients.

The central binomial estimate used in the majorant calculation is
$\binom{2p}{p}\leq 4^p$, rather than the printed $2^p$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.AnalyticRepresentations

/-!
---
title: Factorial estimates for iterated analytic vector fields
type: theorem
---
Suppose the output and all vector-field coefficients admit the same bound
$\alpha C^{|I|}$, where $\alpha,C>0$. For a word of length $p$, its generated
coefficient has absolute value at most $\alpha(2d\alpha C)^p p!$.
Consequently every analytic representation on a finite alphabet has a
uniform factorial bound on its word coefficients.

The central binomial estimate used in the majorant calculation is
$\binom{2p}{p}\leq 4^p$, rather than the printed $2^p$.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.FactorialEstimate

open Lax825748.Series Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation
open ConvergentSeries AnalyticRepresentations

def HasFactorialBound {X : Type} (g : NCSeries X) : Prop :=
  ∃ α : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ w : Word X,
    |g w| ≤ α * C ^ w.toList.length * (w.toList.length.factorial : ℝ)

axiom word_majorant {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (R : Representation X d)
    (α C : ℝ) (hα : 0 < α) (hC : 0 < C)
    (hh : HasGeometricBound R.output α C)
    (hA : ∀ x i, HasGeometricBound (R.fields x i) α C) (w : Word X) :
  |generatingSeries R w| ≤
    α * (2 * (d : ℝ) * α * C) ^ w.toList.length * (w.toList.length.factorial : ℝ)

axiom factorial_bound {X : Type} [Finite X] {d : ℕ}
    (R : Representation X d) (hR : IsAnalytic R) :
  HasFactorialBound (generatingSeries R)

end Lax825748.FactorialEstimate

statements.signature:
factorial_bound : ∀ {X : Type} [Finite X] {d : Nat} (R : Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.Representation X d),
  Lax825748.AnalyticRepresentations.IsAnalytic R →
    Lax825748.FactorialEstimate.HasFactorialBound (Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.generatingSeries R)

word_majorant : ∀ {X : Type} {d : Nat} (R : Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.Representation X d) (α C : Real),
  Real.instLT.lt 0 α →
    Real.instLT.lt 0 C →
      Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.HasGeometricBound R.output α C →
        (∀ (x : X) (i : Fin d), Lax825748.ConvergentSeries.HasGeometricBound (R.fields x i) α C) →
          ∀ (w : Lax825748.Series.Word X),
            Real.instLE.le (abs (Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.generatingSeries R w))
              (instHMul.hMul
                (instHMul.hMul α
                  (instHPow.hPow (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 2 d.cast) α) C)
                    (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe FreeMonoid.toList w).length))
                (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe FreeMonoid.toList w).length.factorial.cast)

concepts.title: Lie rank is the least formal realization dimension
concepts.description:
Every formal differential representation of dimension $e$ generates a series
of finite Lie rank at most $e$. Lie rank $d$ is equivalent to $d$ being
the least dimension of a formal differential
representation. This includes constant series, whose minimal dimension
is zero.

/-!
---
title: Lie rank is the least formal realization dimension
type: theorem
---
Every formal differential representation of dimension $e$ generates a series
of finite Lie rank at most $e$. Lie rank $d$ is equivalent to $d$ being
the least dimension of a formal differential
representation. This includes constant series, whose minimal dimension
is zero.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.FormalMinimality

open Series LieRank DifferentialRepresentation

def IsLeastDimension {X : Type} (g : NCSeries X) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∃ R : Representation X d, Represents R g) ∧
    ∀ e, (∃ R : Representation X e, Represents R g) → d ≤ e

axiom rank_bound {X : Type} {e : ℕ} (R : Representation X e) :
  ∃ d, HasLieRank (generatingSeries R) d ∧ d ≤ e

axiom least_dimension {X : Type} [Finite X] (g : NCSeries X) (d : ℕ) :
  HasLieRank g d ↔ IsLeastDimension g d

end Lax825748.FormalMinimality

concepts.title: Commutative formal series and formal vector fields
concepts.description:
The state algebra in dimension $d$ is $\mathbb R[[q_1,\ldots,q_d]]$.
Its elements are arbitrary commutative formal power series.

A formal vector field with coefficients $\theta_i$ acts on $f$ by
$\sum_i\theta_i\partial_i f$. Formal continuity means continuity for the topology of
agreement of all coefficients below a fixed total degree.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.Monomials
import Mathlib.RingTheory.MvPowerSeries.Derivative

/-!
---
title: Commutative formal series and formal vector fields
type: definition
---
The state algebra in dimension $d$ is $\mathbb R[[q_1,\ldots,q_d]]$.
Its elements are arbitrary commutative formal power series.

A formal vector field with coefficients $\theta_i$ acts on $f$ by
$\sum_i\theta_i\partial_i f$. Formal continuity means continuity for the topology of
agreement of all coefficients below a fixed total degree.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.FormalSeries

open Monomials
open scoped BigOperators

abbrev StateSeries (d : ℕ) := MvPowerSeries (Fin d) ℝ

def AgreeBelow {d : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (f g : StateSeries d) : Prop :=
  ∀ I : Fin d →₀ ℕ, totalDegree I < N →
    MvPowerSeries.coeff I f = MvPowerSeries.coeff I g

def FormallyContinuous {d e : ℕ} (F : StateSeries d → StateSeries e) : Prop :=
  ∀ N, ∃ M, ∀ f g, AgreeBelow M f g → AgreeBelow N (F f) (F g)

abbrev VectorField (d : ℕ) := Fin d → StateSeries d

noncomputable def applyVectorField {d : ℕ} (A : VectorField d)
    (f : StateSeries d) : StateSeries d :=
  ∑ i, A i * MvPowerSeries.pderiv ℝ i f

end Lax825748.FormalSeries

concepts.title: Formal equivalence of minimal realizations
concepts.description:
Two formal differential representations of a series of Lie rank $d$, both of
dimension $d$, are equivalent under a formal change of coordinates
fixing the origin. The change sends the first output series to the second
and intertwines the right action of every word on every state series.
The change of coordinates and its inverse are continuous for the formal topology.

import Lax825748.CoordinateChange

/-!
---
title: Formal equivalence of minimal realizations
type: theorem
---
Two formal differential representations of a series of Lie rank $d$, both of
dimension $d$, are equivalent under a formal change of coordinates
fixing the origin. The change sends the first output series to the second
and intertwines the right action of every word on every state series.
The change of coordinates and its inverse are continuous for the formal topology.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.FormalUniqueness

open Series LieRank DifferentialRepresentation CoordinateChange

axiom minimal_realizations_equivalent {X : Type} [Finite X] {d : ℕ}
    (g : NCSeries X) (hr : HasLieRank g d)
    (R R' : Representation X d) (hR : Represents R g) (hR' : Represents R' g) :
  ∃ φ : FormalChange d,
    φ.toAlgEquiv R.output = R'.output ∧
      ∀ (k : FormalSeries.StateSeries d) (w : Word X),
        φ.toAlgEquiv (act R k w) = act R' (φ.toAlgEquiv k) w

end Lax825748.FormalUniqueness

  Lax825748.LieRank.HasLieRank g d →
    ∀ (R R' : Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.Representation X d),
      Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.Represents R g →
        Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.Represents R' g →
          Exists fun φ =>
            And (Eq (AlgEquiv.instFunLike.coe φ.toAlgEquiv R.output) R'.output)

                  (Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.act R' (AlgEquiv.instFunLike.coe φ.toAlgEquiv k) w))

concepts.title: Lie polynomials and Lie rank
concepts.description:
The Lie polynomials form the Lie subalgebra of $\mathbb R\langle X\rangle$
generated by the letters, with bracket $[P,Q]=PQ-QP$.
The Lie residual space of $g$ is the linear span of the series $P\circ g$
for Lie polynomials $P$. The assertion that $g$ has Lie rank $d$ includes
finite dimensionality; in particular an infinite-dimensional space never
has rank zero by convention.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.Series
import Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.OfAssociative
import Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.Subalgebra
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dimension.Finite

/-!
---
title: Lie polynomials and Lie rank
type: definition
---
The Lie polynomials form the Lie subalgebra of $\mathbb R\langle X\rangle$
generated by the letters, with bracket $[P,Q]=PQ-QP$.
The Lie residual space of $g$ is the linear span of the series $P\circ g$
for Lie polynomials $P$. The assertion that $g$ has Lie rank $d$ includes
finite dimensionality; in particular an infinite-dimensional space never
has rank zero by convention.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.LieRank

open Series

instance polynomialLieRing {X : Type} : LieRing (NCPolynomial X) :=
  LieRing.ofAssociativeRing

def liePolynomials (X : Type) : LieSubalgebra ℝ (NCPolynomial X) :=
  LieSubalgebra.lieSpan ℝ (NCPolynomial X) (Set.range letter)

abbrev LiePolynomial (X : Type) := liePolynomials X

noncomputable def residualSpace {X : Type} (g : NCSeries X) :
    Submodule ℝ (NCSeries X) :=
  Submodule.span ℝ {S | ∃ P : LiePolynomial X, S = leftResidual P.val g}

def HasLieRank {X : Type} (g : NCSeries X) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Module.Finite ℝ (residualSpace g) ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (residualSpace g) = d

def FiniteLieRank {X : Type} (g : NCSeries X) : Prop := ∃ d, HasLieRank g d

end Lax825748.LieRank

concepts.title: Lie rank is the least analytic realization dimension
concepts.description:
A series has Lie rank $d$ and satisfies (C) if and only if $d$ is the
least dimension of its analytic differential representations. The least
dimension is attained. Constant series are included with dimension zero.

concepts.title: Multi-indices and ordered monomials
concepts.description:
For a multi-index $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$, write $|I|=\sum_j i_j$ and
$I!=\prod_j i_j!$. For an ordered family of noncommutative polynomials,
$P^I=P_1^{i_1}\cdots P_d^{i_d}$ uses that order of multiplication.
The empty family has total degree zero, factorial one, and monomial one.

---
title: Multi-indices and ordered monomials
type: definition
---
For a multi-index $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$, write $|I|=\sum_j i_j$ and
$I!=\prod_j i_j!$. For an ordered family of noncommutative polynomials,
$P^I=P_1^{i_1}\cdots P_d^{i_d}$ uses that order of multiplication.
The empty family has total degree zero, factorial one, and monomial one.

namespace Lax825748.Monomials

open Series

def totalDegree {d : ℕ} (I : Fin d → ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ j, I j

def multiFactorial {d : ℕ} (I : Fin d → ℕ) : ℕ := ∏ j, (I j).factorial

noncomputable def orderedPowers {X : Type} {d : ℕ}

  (List.ofFn fun j => P j ^ I j).prod

concepts.description:
Given any totally ordered basis of the Lie polynomials, the nondecreasing
products of its basis elements, including the empty product, form a basis
of the concatenation algebra $\mathbb R\langle X\rangle$.
Linear independence and spanning are stated separately in the conjunction.

import Lax825748.LieRank
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Basis.Defs

/-!
---
title: Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt for Lie polynomials
type: theorem
---
Given any totally ordered basis of the Lie polynomials, the nondecreasing
products of its basis elements, including the empty product, form a basis
of the concatenation algebra $\mathbb R\langle X\rangle$.
Linear independence and spanning are stated separately in the conjunction.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.PBW

open Series LieRank

abbrev OrderedWord (ι : Type) [LinearOrder ι] :=
  {l : List ι // l.Pairwise (· ≤ ·)}

noncomputable def monomial {X ι : Type} [LinearOrder ι]
    (b : Module.Basis ι ℝ (LiePolynomial X)) (l : OrderedWord ι) : NCPolynomial X :=
  (l.val.map fun i => (b i).val).prod

concepts.title: Convergence of PBW coordinate expansions
concepts.description:
Let $P_1,\ldots,P_d$ be a basis modulo a Lie subalgebra $L_0$, and let
$S_1,\ldots,S_d$ be the associated PBW coordinates of
$J^\perp$, where $J=\mathbb R\langle X\rangle L_0$.
If $T\in J^\perp$ satisfies (C), its coordinate expansion is convergent.
The coefficient of $S^I$ is $(T,P^I)/I!$, so (C) is precisely the
required geometric bound for this expansion.

/-!
---
title: The PBW coordinate projection
type: theorem
---
Lemma 7. For the PBW coordinates of a finite-codimension Lie subalgebra,
$$\theta(T)=\sum_I\frac{(T,P^I)}{I!}S^I$$
is a formally continuous shuffle algebra homomorphism. It maps onto
$J^\perp$ and is the identity there.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.Projection

open Series LieRank Monomials Shuffle FormalSeries Annihilator

noncomputable def theta {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X)
    (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) (T : NCSeries X) : NCSeries X :=
  substituteShuffle S (fun I =>
    pairing T (orderedPowers (fun j => (P j).val) I) / (multiFactorial I : ℝ))

axiom projection {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (hP : IsComplement K P)
    (S : Fin d → NCSeries X) (hS : IsCoordinateFamily K P S)
    (hPBW : IsPBWCoordinateFamily P S) :
  Series.FormallyContinuous (theta P S) ∧
  (∀ a : ℝ, theta P S (constantSeries a) = constantSeries a) ∧
  (∀ T U, theta P S (T + U) = theta P S T + theta P S U) ∧
  (∀ T U, theta P S (shuffle T U) = shuffle (theta P S T) (theta P S U)) ∧
  (∀ T, InAnnihilator K (theta P S T)) ∧
  (∀ T, InAnnihilator K T → theta P S T = T)

end Lax825748.Projection

concepts.title: Local analytic realization of generating series
concepts.description:
For a finite alphabet, a real noncommutative series admits an analytic
differential representation if and only if it has finite Lie rank and
satisfies (C). If its Lie rank is $d$, a representation of dimension
exactly $d$ exists.

The realization is obtained in the normalized residual coordinates
$T_i=g\circ Q_i-(g,Q_i)$. Convergence of the output and of the vector-field
coefficients follows from their convergent coordinate expansions.

concepts.title: Noncommutative series and polynomial residuals
concepts.description:
For an alphabet $X$, a series is a function $X^*\to\mathbb R$ and a polynomial
is a finite real linear combination of words. Polynomial multiplication is
concatenation. The pairing is $(S,P)=\sum_w P_w S_w$.

The two residuals are $(S\circ P,w)=(S,Pw)$ and
$(P\circ S,w)=(S,wP)$. The empty word is the monoid identity.
Agreement below degree $N$ means equality at every word of length less than $N$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Algebra.MonoidAlgebra.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.FreeMonoid.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

/-!
---
title: Noncommutative series and polynomial residuals
type: definition
---
For an alphabet $X$, a series is a function $X^*\to\mathbb R$ and a polynomial
is a finite real linear combination of words. Polynomial multiplication is
concatenation. The pairing is $(S,P)=\sum_w P_w S_w$.

The two residuals are $(S\circ P,w)=(S,Pw)$ and
$(P\circ S,w)=(S,wP)$. The empty word is the monoid identity.
Agreement below degree $N$ means equality at every word of length less than $N$.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.Series

abbrev Word (X : Type) := FreeMonoid X
abbrev NCSeries (X : Type) := Word X → ℝ
abbrev NCPolynomial (X : Type) := MonoidAlgebra ℝ (Word X)

noncomputable def pairing {X : Type} (S : NCSeries X) (P : NCPolynomial X) : ℝ :=
  P.coeff.sum fun w a => a * S w

noncomputable def wordPolynomial {X : Type} (w : Word X) : NCPolynomial X :=
  MonoidAlgebra.single w 1

noncomputable def letter {X : Type} (x : X) : NCPolynomial X :=
  wordPolynomial (FreeMonoid.of x)

noncomputable def rightResidual {X : Type} (S : NCSeries X)
    (P : NCPolynomial X) : NCSeries X :=
  fun w => pairing S (P * wordPolynomial w)

noncomputable def leftResidual {X : Type} (P : NCPolynomial X)
    (S : NCSeries X) : NCSeries X :=
  fun w => pairing S (wordPolynomial w * P)

noncomputable def constantSeries {X : Type} (a : ℝ) : NCSeries X := by
  classical
  exact fun w => if w = 1 then a else 0

def AgreeBelow {X : Type} (N : ℕ) (S T : NCSeries X) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, w.toList.length < N → S w = T w

def FormallyContinuous {X Y : Type} (F : NCSeries X → NCSeries Y) : Prop :=
  ∀ N, ∃ M, ∀ S T, AgreeBelow M S T → AgreeBelow N (F S) (F T)

end Lax825748.Series

concepts.title: Shuffle multiplication
concepts.description:
The coefficient of $w$ in the shuffle of $S$ and $T$ is the sum of
$S(w|I)T(w|I^c)$ over subsets of the positions of $w$. Repeated letters retain
their multiplicities. This product is associative and commutative, with unit
the series supported at the empty word. No concatenation product on series
is used here.

import Lax825748.Series

/-!
---
title: Shuffle multiplication
type: definition and theorem
---
The coefficient of $w$ in the shuffle of $S$ and $T$ is the sum of
$S(w|I)T(w|I^c)$ over subsets of the positions of $w$. Repeated letters retain
their multiplicities. This product is associative and commutative, with unit
the series supported at the empty word. No concatenation product on series
is used here.
-/

namespace Lax825748.Shuffle

open Series

def unshuffles {X : Type} : List X → List (List X × List X)
  | [] => [([], [])]
  | x :: w => (unshuffles w).flatMap fun p =>
      [(x :: p.1, p.2), (p.1, x :: p.2)]

noncomputable def shuffle {X : Type} (S T : NCSeries X) : NCSeries X :=
  fun w => ((unshuffles w.toList).map fun p =>
    S (FreeMonoid.ofList p.1) * T (FreeMonoid.ofList p.2)).sum

noncomputable def shuffleList {X : Type} : List (NCSeries X) → NCSeries X
  | [] => constantSeries 1
  | S :: l => shuffle S (shuffleList l)

noncomputable def shufflePow {X : Type} (S : NCSeries X) (n : ℕ) : NCSeries X :=
  shuffleList (List.replicate n S)

axiom commutative {X : Type} (S T : NCSeries X) : shuffle S T = shuffle T S

axiom associative {X : Type} (R S T : NCSeries X) :
  shuffle (shuffle R S) T = shuffle R (shuffle S T)

axiom unit {X : Type} (S : NCSeries X) : shuffle (constantSeries 1) S = S

end Lax825748.Shuffle

concepts.title: Shuffle-finite series
concepts.description:
A series is shuffle finite if it belongs to a finitely generated unital
shuffle subalgebra stable under prefix derivatives. Finite generation is
expressed by spanning all shuffle monomials in a finite family of series.
Only finite linear combinations enter this algebra; its formal completion
is a separate construction.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Span.Defs

/-!
---
title: Shuffle-finite series
type: definition
---
A series is shuffle finite if it belongs to a finitely generated unital
shuffle subalgebra stable under prefix derivatives. Finite generation is
expressed by spanning all shuffle monomials in a finite family of series.
Only finite linear combinations enter this algebra; its formal completion
is a separate construction.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.ShuffleFinite

open Series Shuffle ShuffleIdentities

structure ShuffleSubalgebra (X : Type) where
  toSubmodule : Submodule ℝ (NCSeries X)
  one_mem : constantSeries 1 ∈ toSubmodule
  shuffle_mem : ∀ S T, S ∈ toSubmodule → T ∈ toSubmodule → shuffle S T ∈ toSubmodule

def FinitelyGenerated {X : Type} (A : ShuffleSubalgebra X) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (S : Fin n → NCSeries X),
    A.toSubmodule = Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun I : Fin n → ℕ => shuffleMonomial S I)

def DerivativeStable {X : Type} (A : ShuffleSubalgebra X) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : X) (T : NCSeries X), T ∈ A.toSubmodule →
    rightResidual T (letter x) ∈ A.toSubmodule

def IsShuffleFinite {X : Type} (f : NCSeries X) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : ShuffleSubalgebra X, FinitelyGenerated A ∧ DerivativeStable A ∧ f ∈ A.toSubmodule

end Lax825748.ShuffleFinite

concepts.title: Shuffle-finite coordinates in minimal formal realizations
concepts.description:
If a shuffle-finite series has Lie rank $k$, its minimal formal realization
can be chosen with shuffle-finite coordinate series. They can lie in any
finitely generated, derivative-stable shuffle algebra containing the series.

For a complement $P_j$ to the residual stabilizer, choose polynomials $Q_i$
with $(f,Q_iP_j)=\delta_{ij}$. The coordinate series are
$g_i=f\circ Q_i-(f,Q_i)1$. They belong to the witnessing algebra and give
formal coordinates on the stabilizer ideal's annihilator. This does not
assert polynomial output or transition functions in these coordinates.

import Lax825748.Annihilator
import Lax825748.RepresentationMap

/-!
---
title: Shuffle-finite coordinates in minimal formal realizations
type: theorem
---
If a shuffle-finite series has Lie rank $k$, its minimal formal realization
can be chosen with shuffle-finite coordinate series. They can lie in any
finitely generated, derivative-stable shuffle algebra containing the series.

For a complement $P_j$ to the residual stabilizer, choose polynomials $Q_i$
with $(f,Q_iP_j)=\delta_{ij}$. The coordinate series are
$g_i=f\circ Q_i-(f,Q_i)1$. They belong to the witnessing algebra and give
formal coordinates on the stabilizer ideal's annihilator. This does not
assert polynomial output or transition functions in these coordinates.
-/

namespace Lax825748.ShuffleFiniteCoordinates

open Series ShuffleFinite LieRank Annihilator FormalSeries
open DifferentialRepresentation RepresentationMap

axiom coordinates_in_algebra {X : Type} {k : ℕ} (f : NCSeries X)
    (A : ShuffleSubalgebra X) (hfg : FinitelyGenerated A)
    (hstable : DerivativeStable A) (hf : f ∈ A.toSubmodule)
    (K : LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X)
    (hK : ∀ L : LiePolynomial X, L ∈ K ↔ leftResidual L.val f = 0)
    (P : Fin k → LiePolynomial X) (hP : IsComplement K P) :
    ∃ (Q : Fin k → NCPolynomial X) (G : Fin k → NCSeries X),
      (∀ i, G i = rightResidual f (Q i) - constantSeries (pairing f (Q i))) ∧
      IsCoordinateFamily K P G ∧
      (∀ i, G i ∈ A.toSubmodule ∧ IsShuffleFinite (G i)) ∧
      (∀ T : NCSeries X, InAnnihilator K T ↔
        ∃! u : StateSeries k, substituteShuffle G u = T)

axiom minimal_realization {X : Type} [Finite X] (f : NCSeries X) (k : ℕ)
    (hr : HasLieRank f k) (A : ShuffleSubalgebra X)
    (hfg : FinitelyGenerated A) (hstable : DerivativeStable A) (hf : f ∈ A.toSubmodule) :
    ∃ R : Representation X k, Represents R f ∧
      ∀ i : Fin k, eta R (MvPowerSeries.X i) ∈ A.toSubmodule ∧
        IsShuffleFinite (eta R (MvPowerSeries.X i))

end Lax825748.ShuffleFiniteCoordinates

  Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.FinitelyGenerated A →
    Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.DerivativeStable A →
      SetLike.instMembership.mem A.toSubmodule f →
        ∀ (K : Lax825748.Annihilator.LieSubalgebraOfPolynomials X),
          (∀ (L : Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
              Iff (SetLike.instMembership.mem K L) (Eq (Lax825748.Series.leftResidual L.val f) 0)) →
            ∀ (P : Fin k → Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
              Lax825748.Annihilator.IsComplement K P →
                Exists fun Q =>
                  Exists fun G =>
                    And
                      (∀ (i : Fin k),
                        Eq (G i)
                          (instHSub.hSub (Lax825748.Series.rightResidual f (Q i))
                            (Lax825748.Series.constantSeries (Lax825748.Series.pairing f (Q i)))))
                      (And (Lax825748.Annihilator.IsCoordinateFamily K P G)
                        (And
                          (∀ (i : Fin k),
                            And (SetLike.instMembership.mem A.toSubmodule (G i))
                              (Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.IsShuffleFinite (G i)))
                          (∀ (T : Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
                            Iff (Lax825748.Annihilator.InAnnihilator K T)
                              (ExistsUnique fun u => Eq (Lax825748.Annihilator.substituteShuffle G u) T))))

minimal_realization : ∀ {X : Type} [Finite X] (f : Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X) (k : Nat),
  Lax825748.LieRank.HasLieRank f k →
    ∀ (A : Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.ShuffleSubalgebra X),
      Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.FinitelyGenerated A →
        Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.DerivativeStable A →
          SetLike.instMembership.mem A.toSubmodule f →
            Exists fun R =>
              And (Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.Represents R f)

                    (Lax825748.ShuffleFinite.IsShuffleFinite (Lax825748.RepresentationMap.eta R (MvPowerSeries.X i))))

concepts.title: Coproduct and shuffle identities
concepts.description:
Lemmas 1–5. The $p$-fold coproduct assigns each position of a word to one
of $p$ tensor factors. Tensor polynomials are represented by finite linear
combinations of $p$-tuples of words. Its value on a letter is the sum of the
$p$ placements of that letter, and Lie polynomials are primitive.

Pairing with this coproduct computes the shuffle product. Letter residuals
are derivations. A shuffle product of $i$ zero-constant series vanishes on
a product of fewer than $i$ Lie polynomials. For equal numbers of factors,
the pairing is the sum over permutations of pairwise evaluations.

For normalized coordinate series, equal-degree monomials have diagonal
pairing $I!=\prod_i I_i!$ and off-diagonal pairing zero. This corrects
the printed $|I|!$ in Lemma 5(ii).
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.Shuffle
import Lax825748.LieRank
import Lax825748.Monomials
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Perm

/-!
---
title: Coproduct and shuffle identities
type: theorem
---
Lemmas 1–5. The $p$-fold coproduct assigns each position of a word to one
of $p$ tensor factors. Tensor polynomials are represented by finite linear
combinations of $p$-tuples of words. Its value on a letter is the sum of the
$p$ placements of that letter, and Lie polynomials are primitive.

Pairing with this coproduct computes the shuffle product. Letter residuals
are derivations. A shuffle product of $i$ zero-constant series vanishes on
a product of fewer than $i$ Lie polynomials. For equal numbers of factors,
the pairing is the sum over permutations of pairwise evaluations.

For normalized coordinate series, equal-degree monomials have diagonal
pairing $I!=\prod_i I_i!$ and off-diagonal pairing zero. This corrects
the printed $|I|!$ in Lemma 5(ii).
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities

open Series Shuffle LieRank Monomials
open scoped BigOperators

abbrev TensorPolynomial (X : Type) (p : ℕ) :=
  MonoidAlgebra ℝ (Fin p → Word X)

def distributions {X : Type} (p : ℕ) : List X → List (Fin p → List X)
  | [] => [fun _ => []]
  | x :: w => (distributions p w).flatMap fun v =>
      List.ofFn fun i : Fin p => Function.update v i (x :: v i)

noncomputable def coproduct {X : Type} (p : ℕ) (P : NCPolynomial X) :
    TensorPolynomial X p :=
  P.coeff.sum fun w a => ((distributions p w.toList).map fun v =>
    MonoidAlgebra.single (fun i => FreeMonoid.ofList (v i)) a).sum

noncomputable def tensorPairing {X : Type} {p : ℕ} (S : Fin p → NCSeries X)
    (P : TensorPolynomial X p) : ℝ :=
  P.coeff.sum fun v a => a * ∏ i, S i (v i)

noncomputable def insertFactor {X : Type} {p : ℕ} (i : Fin p)
    (P : NCPolynomial X) : TensorPolynomial X p :=
  P.coeff.sum fun w a => MonoidAlgebra.single (fun j => if j = i then w else 1) a

axiom coproduct_multiplicative {X : Type} (p : ℕ) (P Q : NCPolynomial X) :
  coproduct p (P * Q) = coproduct p P * coproduct p Q

axiom pairing_coproduct {X : Type} {p : ℕ} (S : Fin p → NCSeries X)
    (P : NCPolynomial X) :
  pairing (shuffleList (List.ofFn S)) P = tensorPairing S (coproduct p P)

axiom lie_primitive {X : Type} (p : ℕ) (P : LiePolynomial X) :
  coproduct p P.val = ∑ i : Fin p, insertFactor i P.val

axiom residual_derivation {X : Type} (x : X) (S T : NCSeries X) :
  rightResidual (shuffle S T) (letter x) =
    shuffle (rightResidual S (letter x)) T + shuffle S (rightResidual T (letter x))

axiom vanishing {X : Type} {i j : ℕ} (hji : j < i)
    (T : Fin i → NCSeries X) (hT : ∀ k, T k 1 = 0)
    (Q : Fin j → LiePolynomial X) :
  pairing (shuffleList (List.ofFn T)) ((List.ofFn fun k => (Q k).val).prod) = 0

axiom permutation_pairing {X : Type} {n : ℕ}
    (T : Fin n → NCSeries X) (hT : ∀ k, T k 1 = 0)
    (Q : Fin n → LiePolynomial X) :
  pairing (shuffleList (List.ofFn T)) ((List.ofFn fun k => (Q k).val).prod) =
    ∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∏ k, pairing (T k) (Q (σ k)).val

noncomputable def shuffleMonomial {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (S : Fin d → NCSeries X)
    (I : Fin d → ℕ) : NCSeries X :=
  shuffleList (List.ofFn fun i => shufflePow (S i) (I i))

axiom triangular_pairing {X : Type} {d : ℕ} (S : Fin d → NCSeries X)
    (P : Fin d → LiePolynomial X) (hS : ∀ i, S i 1 = 0)
    (hSP : ∀ i j, pairing (S i) (P j).val = if i = j then 1 else 0)
    (I J : Fin d → ℕ) :
  (totalDegree J < totalDegree I →
    pairing (shuffleMonomial S I) (orderedPowers (fun i => (P i).val) J) = 0) ∧
  (totalDegree I = totalDegree J →
    pairing (shuffleMonomial S I) (orderedPowers (fun i => (P i).val) J) =
      if I = J then (multiFactorial I : ℝ) else 0)

end Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities

coproduct_multiplicative : ∀ {X : Type} (p : Nat) (P Q : Lax825748.Series.NCPolynomial X),
  Eq (Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities.coproduct p (instHMul.hMul P Q))
    (instHMul.hMul (Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities.coproduct p P) (Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities.coproduct p Q))

lie_primitive : ∀ {X : Type} (p : Nat) (P : Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
  Eq (Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities.coproduct p P.val)
    (Finset.univ.sum fun i => Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities.insertFactor i P.val)

pairing_coproduct : ∀ {X : Type} {p : Nat} (S : Fin p → Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X) (P : Lax825748.Series.NCPolynomial X),
  Eq (Lax825748.Series.pairing (Lax825748.Shuffle.shuffleList (List.ofFn S)) P)
    (Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities.tensorPairing S (Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities.coproduct p P))

permutation_pairing : ∀ {X : Type} {n : Nat} (T : Fin n → Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
  (∀ (k : Fin n), Eq (T k 1) 0) →
    ∀ (Q : Fin n → Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
      Eq (Lax825748.Series.pairing (Lax825748.Shuffle.shuffleList (List.ofFn T)) (List.ofFn fun k => (Q k).val).prod)
        (Finset.univ.sum fun σ =>
          Finset.univ.prod fun k => Lax825748.Series.pairing (T k) (Q (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe σ k)).val)

residual_derivation : ∀ {X : Type} (x : X) (S T : Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
  Eq (Lax825748.Series.rightResidual (Lax825748.Shuffle.shuffle S T) (Lax825748.Series.letter x))
    (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax825748.Shuffle.shuffle (Lax825748.Series.rightResidual S (Lax825748.Series.letter x)) T)
      (Lax825748.Shuffle.shuffle S (Lax825748.Series.rightResidual T (Lax825748.Series.letter x))))

triangular_pairing : ∀ {X : Type} {d : Nat} (S : Fin d → Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X)
  (P : Fin d → Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
  (∀ (i : Fin d), Eq (S i 1) 0) →
    (∀ (i j : Fin d), Eq (Lax825748.Series.pairing (S i) (P j).val) (ite (Eq i j) 1 0)) →
      ∀ (I J : Fin d → Nat),
        And
          (instLTNat.lt (Lax825748.Monomials.totalDegree J) (Lax825748.Monomials.totalDegree I) →
            Eq
              (Lax825748.Series.pairing (Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities.shuffleMonomial S I)
                (Lax825748.Monomials.orderedPowers (fun i => (P i).val) J))
              0)
          (Eq (Lax825748.Monomials.totalDegree I) (Lax825748.Monomials.totalDegree J) →
            Eq
              (Lax825748.Series.pairing (Lax825748.ShuffleIdentities.shuffleMonomial S I)
                (Lax825748.Monomials.orderedPowers (fun i => (P i).val) J))
              (ite (Eq I J) (Lax825748.Monomials.multiFactorial I).cast 0))

vanishing : ∀ {X : Type} {i j : Nat},
  instLTNat.lt j i →
    ∀ (T : Fin i → Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
      (∀ (k : Fin i), Eq (T k 1) 0) →
        ∀ (Q : Fin j → Subtype fun x => SetLike.instMembership.mem (Lax825748.LieRank.LiePolynomial X) x),
          Eq
            (Lax825748.Series.pairing (Lax825748.Shuffle.shuffleList (List.ofFn T)) (List.ofFn fun k => (Q k).val).prod)
            0

concepts.title: Analytic equivalence of minimal realizations
concepts.description:
Two analytic differential representations of a series of Lie rank $d$,
both of dimension $d$, are related by an analytic change of coordinates
fixing the origin. This change sends the first output to the second and
intertwines the action of every word on every state series.
Its inverse is also convergent and formally continuous.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax825748.Minimality
import Lax825748.AnalyticChanges
import Lax825748.FormalUniqueness

/-!
---
title: Analytic equivalence of minimal realizations
type: theorem
---
Two analytic differential representations of a series of Lie rank $d$,
both of dimension $d$, are related by an analytic change of coordinates
fixing the origin. This change sends the first output to the second and
intertwines the action of every word on every state series.
Its inverse is also convergent and formally continuous.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace Lax825748.Uniqueness

open Lax825748.Series Lax825748.LieRank Lax825748.FormalSeries
open Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation AnalyticRepresentations AnalyticChanges

axiom minimal_realizations_equivalent {X : Type} [Finite X] {d : ℕ}
    (g : NCSeries X) (hr : HasLieRank g d)
    (R R' : Representation X d) (hR : Represents R g) (hR' : Represents R' g)
    (ha : IsAnalytic R) (ha' : IsAnalytic R') :
  ∃ φ : AnalyticChange d,
    φ.toAlgEquiv R.output = R'.output ∧
      ∀ (k : StateSeries d) (w : Word X),
        φ.toAlgEquiv (act R k w) = act R' (φ.toAlgEquiv k) w

end Lax825748.Uniqueness

statements.signature:
minimal_realizations_equivalent : ∀ {X : Type} [Finite X] {d : Nat} (g : Lax825748.Series.NCSeries X),
  Lax825748.LieRank.HasLieRank g d →
    ∀ (R R' : Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.Representation X d),
      Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.Represents R g →
        Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.Represents R' g →
          Lax825748.AnalyticRepresentations.IsAnalytic R →
            Lax825748.AnalyticRepresentations.IsAnalytic R' →
              Exists fun φ =>
                And (Eq (AlgEquiv.instFunLike.coe φ.toAlgEquiv R.output) R'.output)
                  (∀ (k : Lax825748.FormalSeries.StateSeries d) (w : Lax825748.Series.Word X),
                    Eq (AlgEquiv.instFunLike.coe φ.toAlgEquiv (Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.act R k w))
                      (Lax825748.DifferentialRepresentation.act R' (AlgEquiv.instFunLike.coe φ.toAlgEquiv k) w))

proofs.description:
A geometric coefficient bound is summable after reducing the polyradius.
Conversely, the sum of absolute terms bounds each weighted coefficient.

The coordinate expressions in PBW coordinates converge. Transfer from the
given coordinates to PBW coordinates is a formal change with convergent
coordinate images. Apply analytic inversion and convergent composition.

Conjugate the coordinate derivations by the formal automorphism. Their
coefficients form the inverse Jacobian, which converges by the adjugate
formula and reciprocal convergence. The factorial estimate for these vector
fields bounds the Taylor coefficients of each inverse coordinate geometrically.

The defining ideal is a left ideal, so its annihilator is invariant under
right residuals.

The coproduct of each generator of the defining left ideal is primitive;
every term therefore has a factor annihilated by one of the series.

Take the coefficients dual to the degree-one complement monomials in an
adapted PBW basis. They vanish on all monomials containing a stabilizer factor.

Extend the prescribed coordinates inside the shuffle algebra to a chart on
its common Lie stabilizer. Pull back the algebra, adjoin the reciprocal of
the frame determinant, and set the extra variables to zero.

Choose normalized residual coordinates in the witnessing shuffle algebra.
The output and every coordinate residual pull back into the common CDA
algebra supplied by the coordinate theorem.

Shrink the target polyradius until each substituted coordinate has weighted
absolute sum at most a convergence radius of the input. Polynomial truncations
then have uniformly bounded coefficients, and formal continuity transfers the
bound to the full substituted series.

Coefficient convolution preserves geometric bounds after enlarging the
geometric constant. Addition and constants obey the same condition.

Use normalized, centered polynomial residuals as coordinates on the
residual-kernel annihilator. Both the output and the letter residuals of
the coordinates satisfy (C), so their coordinate expressions converge.

Choose one geometric coefficient bound for the output and the finitely
many vector-field coefficients, and apply the word majorant.

The product of factorials divides the total factorial. The multinomial
coefficient is one nonnegative summand in the multinomial expansion of
the power of the number of variables.

Absorb the exponential factor in the factorial comparison into the
geometric constant. Using $q+1$ also covers the empty family.

The finite coefficient system is triangular with nonzero factorial diagonal.
Solve it degree by degree, then use the adapted PBW basis to identify series
in the annihilator from their complementary moments.

FormalExistence in the Lie-rank dimension and the general rank bound give the two
directions of the characterization.
The rank bound applies to every representation, while existence attains it.

In minimal dimension the tangent residual map is onto. Consequently each
representation's series homomorphism is a continuous algebra isomorphism
onto the same residual-kernel annihilator. Compose these isomorphisms.

Every finite family of Lie polynomials acts by convergent vector fields.
Apply the factorial estimate to this finite alphabet, then compare the
total factorial with the multi-index factorial.

Shuffle pairings separate the ordered monomials. Reordering adjacent basis
elements changes a product only by terms of lower Lie degree, which proves
spanning by induction on that degree.

The PBW coefficient formula divides the bound in (C) by the positive
multi-index factorial, leaving a geometric coefficient bound.

PBW-dual coordinates give a diagonal moment matrix: a shuffle monomial pairs
only with its matching complementary PBW monomial, with factorial value.

Expand the coproduct over assignments of Lie factors to tensor slots.
Nonsurjective assignments vanish, and the bijective ones are permutations.

Differentiation multiplies a coefficient by at most $|I|+1\leq 2^{|I|}$;
enlarging the geometric constant preserves convergence.

The PBW expansion preserves complementary moments. Those moments determine
annihilator series and determine the moments of shuffle products by the
primitive coproduct. Finite truncations give formal continuity.

Every Lie residual is a linear combination of the $d$ tangent-output series
obtained by differentiating the output trajectories at the origin.

Combine the formal rank bound, necessity of (C), and analytic existence in
the Lie-rank dimension.

Every analytic representation obeys the formal rank bound. Analytic
existence attains that bound, and necessity supplies (C).
Subtracting the constant term preserves the convergence condition.

Prepend a letter to the tested Lie family, with exponent one. Iteration
gives word residuals, and linearity gives every polynomial residual.

Choose finite polynomial functionals dual to a basis of the Lie residual
space. Centered prefix residuals belong to the witnessing algebra and form
a normalized coordinate family on the stabilizer annihilator.

Use the Lie residual kernel and a complement of size equal to the Lie rank.
The shuffle-finite normalized coordinates give a formal representation whose
state-coordinate series are exactly the chosen residual coordinates.

Expand each multi-index into its list of repeated labels. Below the diagonal
use vanishing; on the diagonal the surviving permutations preserve labels,
so their number is the product of the factorials of the multiplicities.

The formal equivalence identifies the two representation maps onto their
common annihilator. Their coordinate series satisfy (C); the analytic
coordinate theorem makes the equivalence and its inverse convergent.

In the coproduct expansion, fewer Lie factors than tensor slots leave an
empty slot in every term. A zero constant coefficient kills that term.

Use the nonnegative series $F_I=C^{|I|}$ as a coefficient majorant.
Its derivatives satisfy $\partial_i F\preceq C F^2$. After $p$ vector
fields the majorant is $\alpha(2d\alpha C)^p p! F^{2p+1}$; its constant
coefficient is the claimed bound.
